root_cause.text: Use of sprintf (unbounded string formatting) into fixed-size stack buffers without size checking in the SIP and Amanda NAT helpers, specifically in `mangle_content_len()` where the buffer was too small to hold the maximum possible integer value, causing a stack buffer overflow.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `sprintf` with `scnprintf` and adds a size parameter to `sip_sprintf_addr` and `sip_sprintf_addr_port`. In `mangle_content_len()`, the buffer was increased from `sizeof("65536")` (7 bytes) to `sizeof("4294967295")` (11 bytes) to accommodate the full range of a 32-bit unsigned integer. The KASAN stack-out-of-bounds trace in the CVE description points to `sprintf` called from `mangle_content_len`, confirming the overflow.
